text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Lisbon's new airport will be ready in the year 2007 and will involve a partnership between public and private capital and an investment of more than 350 billion escudos.
- After intense negotiatons between the Portuguese government and the European Commission, previously announced 20 percent cuts on subsidies to cereal farmers will not occur.
- Banco Espirito Santo denied accusations levied by members of the Simon Wiesenthal centre that it helped "launder" illicit Nazi gold during World War Two.
- Philips says it will build a new battery factory in Ovar, central Portugal, involving an investment of two billion escudos.
- Saudi Aramco will buy a 27.5 percent stake in oil company Petrogal, a government source told the newspaper.
- Bad debts of the five biggest Portuguese banking groups fell to 5.98 percent in 1995 from 5.1 percent in 1996, according to a study by international accounting firm KPMG.
